comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.academicYear: Current 2026-2027 curriculum for students starting in 2026; checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum explicitly establishes a three-year, 180-EC programme: a 60-EC first-year core; a 30-EC specialisation plus 15 EC of compulsory choices and 15 EC of elective/profile space in year two; and Thesis Lab, a bachelor thesis and 45 EC of profile space in year three. The Social Life of English is selected because its mix of historical sociolinguistics, language and identity, varieties of English and World Englishes most broadly represents the programme title's combined language-and-culture identity. Genuine profile space is preserved rather than filled with invented courses, and restricted choices are instantiated neutrally from the official display order where possible.

candidates.label: Language learning and teaching across the lifespan

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the general English Language and Culture bachelor rather than one specialisation. Among the five official specialisations, The Social Life of English most broadly preserves the programme title's combined language-and-culture identity through historical sociolinguistics, language and identity, sociolinguistic variation and World Englishes. This selection is made independently of UCR course fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two feasible, generator-backed directions: a combined literature/self/transforming-texts pathway and an English/identity/global-culture pathway. Each changes at least 30 EC from every other route, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached. Language Learning and Teaching across the Lifespan is not feasible because UCR lacks a sustained second-language-acquisition and language-pedagogy sequence; Celtic Literatures and Linguistics is not feasible because UCR offers neither medieval Irish or Welsh nor a Celtic philology and literary-history sequence.

alternatives.label: English literature, culture & language
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum balances English-language literature and cultural analysis with language, communication, sociolinguistic context and independent research.
alternatives.concept: A broad English studies pathway combining literary interpretation across periods and media with cultural history, language and communication, identity, social context, psycholinguistics and qualitative and historical research.
progression: Introductory literature, rhetoric, brain and behaviour, history, sociology, media and politics precede advanced literary, cultural, communication and psycholinguistic work. Research Methods & Statistics and qualitative methods precede advanced historical and literary research. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & transforming texts
alternatives.labelReason: The route is organised around literary interpretation, film, media, adaptation, art, cultural theory and creative production, directly reflecting the two literature-led specialisations.
alternatives.concept: A humanities-led English studies direction focused on literature, interpretation and transformation across film, media, art and creative communication, with cultural history, identity and research methods supporting advanced work.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces politics, international relations, psycholinguistics and advanced history with media archaeology, environmental media, documentary, advanced art-historical methods and a denser sequence in literary and visual transformation. Eight of 24 courses differ, a 60-EC change.
progression: Introductory literature, film and media, rhetoric, history, art history, sociology and research methods precede literary theory, adaptation, documentary, race and media, creative communication and art-historical research. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

alternatives.label: English, identity & global culture
alternatives.labelReason: The route foregrounds language, identity, social belonging and global cultural circulation through communication, sociology, media, history, politics and psycholinguistics.
alternatives.concept: A social and cultural English studies direction centred on language, identity and belonging, supported by rhetoric, sociology, global politics, media representation, histories of gender and Indigenous experience, creative communication and psycholinguistics.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces four literature, art and international-relations courses with environmental media, advanced social theory, Native American history and a focused social-identity psychology course. Compared with the literature-and-media route, eight courses differ. The organising emphasis is social variation, identity and global cultural life.
progression: Foundations in communication, sociology, literature, media, modern history and politics precede advanced social theory, identity and media, Indigenous history, creative communication and psycholinguistics. Qualitative and statistical foundations precede advanced research. All prerequisites and planned-semester constraints are satisfied.

notes.text: Utrecht provides a fixed first-year English core, a formal 30-EC specialisation, 60 EC of genuine profile space and a dedicated Thesis Lab and bachelor thesis. UCR can build coherent literature/culture/language, transforming-texts and language/identity pathways, but it does not reproduce Utrecht's compulsory English phonetics, grammar, morphosyntax, historical sociolinguistics and World Englishes sequence or its dedicated thesis structure.
